summary: External KV-prefetch to tool-proxy over TLS inflates tail latency and triggers streaming timeouts
description:
Issue summary:
Customer NovaRetail reports elevated p99 end-to-end request latency and recurring streaming disconnects when using function/tool calling with KV-prefetch enabled. Problem appears correlated with requests that trigger a preflight fetch of tool metadata/KV from an external proxy endpoint that uses mutual TLS. Impact:
- ~3-5% of streaming generation sessions for NovaRetail hit end-to-end timeouts (~30s) and disconnects during peak traffic windows (13:00-15:00 UTC).
- Tail latency (p99/p999) for affected routes increased by 400-900ms.
- Customers on dedicated capacity experiencing highest impact due to strict SLOs; self-serve customers unaffected in current report.
Environment:
- prod/us-east-1, dedicated pool for NovaRetail, serving-runtime v3.4.1, function-proxy v1.7.0, schema-validator v0.9.2.
Observed behavior:
- Requests that require KV-prefetch to external tool-proxy perform a synchronous TLS-backed HTTP call before streaming starts. In many cases TLS handshake + TCP + DNS/resolution adds a variable 200-800ms extra per request. Occasionally an initial TLS negotiation fails and a retry occurs, adding ~1.2s. When request arrives with long generation sequences this leads to streaming start delays, and on some clients results in client-side timeout and reconnect.
Why this ticket exists:
- Customer impacted in production with visible errors and business impact; support engaged to coordinate SRE/Eng mitigation and longer-term fix.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Provision a dedicated tenant with KV-prefetch and tool call enabled (matches NovaRetail config).
2) Use serving-runtime v3.4.1 and function-proxy v1.7.0.
3) Drive 200 RPS against /v1/chat/completions with streaming enabled and calls resolved to tool proxy endpoint (third-party host).
4) Observe latency histograms for streaming start and watch for streaming disconnects/timeouts in the first-token timing.
5) Re-run with KV-prefetch disabled (or using local stub proxy) to compare tail latency differential.

investigation_notes:
Initial triage (Support): confirmed issue correlates with KV-prefetch + external tool-proxy domain. Customer traces show synchronous preflight before streaming handshake.
SRE observed increased DNS resolution latency (sporadic 50-300ms) for the external proxy during peak. Packet captures show occasional TLS 0-RTT rejected and full handshake fallback.
Hypotheses considered:
- DNS resolution/backoff causing variability (likely).
- External proxy performing client cert renegotiation forcing full TLS handshake (observed hints).
- Our client uses blocking prefetch (synchronous) which amplifies the handshake cost and becomes part of e2e path (architectural issue).
Partial findings:
- Reproduced p99 delta locally by pointing runtime at a testproxy with similar TLS behavior.
- Disabling KV-prefetch or using an internal stub proxy reduced p99 by ~650ms and eliminated observed streaming disconnects in load test.
- function-proxy logs show blocking behavior: preflight call completes before stream socket is created. This matches code path in tool-proxies client (syncFetchKV in toolcall-handler).
Next steps agreed:
- Short term: toggle to make KV-prefetch asynchronous when streaming is requested (hotfix toggle).
- Mid term: add local caching for KV metadata and fallback immediately to cached/empty metadata if external fetch exceeds 200ms.
- Long term: redesign preflight to avoid blocking streaming socket creation; move preflight to parallel path or streaming preamble.
Engineering owner: Ethan Zhang (serving-runtime), Proxy owner: Marina Kovacs (tool-proxies).
comments: Priya Menon (Support) - 2026-03-12: Customer reports intermittent streaming disconnects. Attached request-ids and sample logs. Marking P1 due to business impact.
Ethan Zhang (SRE) - 2026-03-12: Started collecting distributed traces and p99 histograms. Early signal points to kv-prefetch over external proxy; filing for deeper debug.

Marina Kovacs (Proxy Team) - 2026-03-13: Observed TLS client-cert renegotiation on some upstream nodes; coordinating with infra to rotate certs and check mTLS configs. Also seeing intermittent DNS TTL issues for proxy-egress host.
Priya Menon (Support) - 2026-03-13: Provided customer traffic windows and confirmed impact is repeatable during their peak. Customer accepted temporary opt-out of KV-prefetch for affected route.
Ethan Zhang (SRE) - 2026-03-14: Deployed feature-flag that makes kv-prefetch non-blocking for streaming endpoints (canary to 10% of NovaRetail traffic). Monitoring for errors and p99 improvements.
Marina Kovacs (Proxy Team) - 2026-03-14: Rolling certificate remediation for problematic proxy nodes; DNS cache TTL lowered and health-checks increased. Will follow up with PR link for config change.
resolution:
Mitigation applied: feature-flag enabled to make KV-prefetch non-blocking for streaming routes and an emergency cache fallback was added to return cached metadata if external fetch exceeds 200ms. Certificate remediation and DNS adjustments performed on proxy fleet.
Permanent fix: engineering to implement non-blocking preflight pipeline, local KV metadata cache with staleness policy, and improved observability for preflight latency. Targeted PRs: serving-runtime PR #1298 (non-blocking preflight), tool-proxies PR #342 (mTLS config and health-checks).
Follow-ups:
- Monitor NovaRetail p99 and error rate for 72 hours post-change.
- Create task to backfill automated test that simulates expensive TLS handshake and validates non-blocking behavior.
- Postmortem and runbook update scheduled after stabilization.
